newsitem.title: FRANCE: CLF-Dexia France says activity picking up.
newsitem.headline: CLF-Dexia France says activity picking up.

text.p: Credit Local de France-Groupe Dexia, the French arm of Franco-Belgian banking group Dexia, said on Tuesday that it had registered 29.75 billion francs in new local authority financing in the first four months of 1997.
CLF-Groupe Dexia said in a statement, issued on the day of its annual shareholders' meeting, that activity was picking up in France.
"By the end of the year Groupe Dexia should hit 100 billion francs in new credits," the statement said.
"We expect to continue a dynamic dividend distribution policy in the years to come," CLF chairman Pierre Richard said in the statement.
CLF-Dexia France, which is changing its name to Dexia-France, proposed a net dividend of 15.70 francs per share for 1996, up 13 percent on 1995.
